clue.text: Patient starts with cure incomplete at this stage

definitions.text: Patient starts with cure incomplete at this stage

indicators.note: the opening letter of the word Patient is what this signals, a patient's start
the synonym for cure loses its final letter, so it is left unfinished

parts.note: a cure is a remedy

explanation.surface: A hospital patient begins treatment before the cure is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the sedation given at the beginning of an operation, before any cure arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Premedication is the sedative a patient is given at the start, before surgery begins.

clue.text: Pace bid failing with zero carbon vehicle

indicators.note: a failing bid collapses, so the letters of these two words fall into a new order

explanation.surface: A bid to set the pace collapses, along with an eco-friendly car.
explanation.walkthrough: 'failing' rearranges PACEBID.
explanation.definitionFit: A pedal-powered rickshaw burns no fuel, so it is a vehicle with no carbon emissions.

clue.text: Duck one found in German dam

indicators.note: one piece is discovered sitting within the other, so the letter goes inside

parts.note: the Eder dam in Germany, famous from the Dambusters raid
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A bird is discovered at a reservoir in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: 'found in' puts I inside EDER. The Eder was one of the dams breached in the 1943 Dambusters raid.
explanation.definitionFit: The eider is a large sea duck prized for its soft down.

clue.text: Unreliable niche vehicle flogged in Mexico stalls?

indicators.note: something unreliable cannot be trusted to stay put, so the word's letters are rearranged

parts.note: a Lada is a Russian car, a byword for unreliability

explanation.surface: A car with a poor reputation is sold off at Mexican markets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unreliable' rearranges NICHE to ENCHI. 'flogged' is British slang for sold; it looks like a beating but is part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Tortilla rolls with filling are a staple sold by Mexican street vendors.

clue.text: Disturbing crime account in China

indicators.note: disturbing things shakes them up, so these letters are set in a new order

explanation.surface: An upsetting crime is reported in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disturbing' rearranges CRIME plus AC. 'China' looks like the country but means porcelain.
explanation.definitionFit: China is fired porcelain, a kind of pottery or earthenware.

clue.text: A bit of music for mad dance in church

indicators.note: the jumbled dance is placed within the abbreviation for church

parts.note: CE stands for Church of England

indicators.note: something mad is wildly disordered, so the word's letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: A snatch of music accompanies a frenzied dance in church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mad' scrambles the dance, and 'in' places the result inside the Church of England abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A cadence is a closing sequence of chords, a short passage of a piece.

clue.text: Ill-feeling not good for a Dickensian

indicators.note: the clue says to go without one letter, so it is dropped

parts.note: a grudge is lasting ill-feeling

explanation.surface: Bad blood that isn't kindly, as in a Dickens novel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes G from GRUDGE. Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby Rudge is a character, and title, from Charles Dickens's fiction.

clue.text: Lasting entertainment of resort to gin by doctor

parts.note: MO is Medical Officer, a military doctor
to resort to something is to use it
a gin is a snare or trap for animals

explanation.surface: Someone takes to drink on medical advice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gin' means a snare here, not the drink. The pieces read in the order MO, USE, TRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: Agatha Christie's play has run in London's West End since 1952, the longest run of any stage show.

clue.text: Soldier in action has to double up

indicators.note: the soldier is placed within the word for action

parts.note: a legal action is a case
RE is the Royal Engineers, standing for a soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier in battle has to bend over double.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' means a lawsuit, not combat; 'in' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: To fold something so it doubles over leaves a line or fold in it.

clue.text: G & T does transform dull food

indicators.note: transforming something changes its shape, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A gin and tonic makes bland food bearable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'transform' rearranges G, T and DOES.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, filling, unexciting food such as suet pudding.

clue.text: English addicted possibly to being set apart for a purpose

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: An addicted Englishman is perhaps devoted to one aim.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges E plus ADDICTED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dedicated has been reserved or consecrated for one particular use.

clue.text: Adherent of religion from 6 part 1

parts.note: the first part of 6-down MOUSETRAP is MO plus USE; MO, medical officer, is a doctor, abbreviated DR
the first part of 6-down MOUSETRAP is MO plus USE; MO, medical officer, is a doctor, abbreviated DR

explanation.surface: A believer drawn from the opening of a long-running play.
explanation.walkthrough: The first part of the 6-down answer splits as MO and USE; MO is swapped for its equivalent, Dr, the short form of doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: The Druze are a monotheistic religious community of Syria, Lebanon and Israel, so one member is a follower of that faith.

clue.text: Blimey — soldier chasing a dog!

indicators.note: chasing means coming after, so the soldier follows the exclamation

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise, like blimey
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: An exclamation as a soldier runs after a dog.
explanation.walkthrough: 'chasing' means coming behind, so the soldier follows the exclamation; cor is British slang for surprise.
explanation.definitionFit: A corgi is a small Welsh herding breed, famously kept by the Queen.

clue.text: Muck-spreading sense in Kent

parts.note: muck is dung, manure

indicators.note: spreading scatters things about, so the word's letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Smelling manure being spread in the Kent countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muck-spreading' reads as one farming term but splits in two, with 'spreading' scrambling the following word.
explanation.definitionFit: Dungeness is a shingle headland on the Kent coast, so the place lies in that county.

clue.text: Saucy female prone to disappear in "Carousel"

definitions.meaning: an old word for a cheeky or disreputable young woman
luggage on an airport carousel that tends to go missing

explanation.walkthrough: The quotation marks suggest the musical Carousel, but it is the airport luggage belt.
explanation.definitionFit: Baggage is both luggage and a dated term for an impudent woman.

clue.text: Envious author on "The Old 500"

parts.note: Graham Greene, the English novelist
ye is an old form of the
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A novelist writes about a vintage car race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Old 500' looks like a title, but splits as YE (old 'the') and D (500).
explanation.definitionFit: Green-eyed is the jealous state, from Shakespeare's green-eyed monster.

clue.text: Lady's partner undoes corset

indicators.note: undoing the garment unpicks it, so its letters come apart and are rearranged

explanation.surface: A woman's companion unlaces her corset.
explanation.walkthrough: 'undoes' rearranges CORSET.
explanation.definitionFit: An escort is a man who accompanies a woman to a social event.

clue.text: Locust tree fruit — get one for nothing in the West Indies

indicators.note: the letter for nothing is swapped out and the letter for one put in its place

parts.note: the carob is also called the locust tree
a bean is the fruit or seed of a pod

explanation.surface: A fruit that comes free with a purchase in the Caribbean.
explanation.walkthrough: One is I and nothing is O, so the O of CAROB BEAN becomes I. 'get one for nothing' reads like a shop offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean is the sea and island region that includes the West Indies.

clue.text: King James version in Jude — perhaps you've seen it all before

indicators.note: the Bible version sits within the rearranged name
perhaps suggests the name may be reordered

parts.note: AV is the Authorised Version, the King James Bible

explanation.surface: Reading the Epistle of Jude in the King James Bible feels familiar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' scrambles the name and 'in' places the Bible abbreviation inside it; Jude is a book of the New Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Déjà vu is the uncanny feeling that a new experience has happened previously.

clue.text: Stranger sometimes referred to as "x"'

definitions.meaning: in algebra x is the quantity yet to be found

explanation.definitionFit: Unknown means both an unfamiliar person and an algebraic variable to be solved for.

clue.text: Praises false deity

indicators.note: false means not genuine, so the letters are put in another order

explanation.surface: Worship offered to an idol rather than a true god.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' rearranges PRAISES; 'false deity' reads as one phrase but 'false' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Serapis was a Graeco-Egyptian god worshipped in Ptolemaic Alexandria.

clue.text: Possible euphemism for that is a serious crime

definitions.text: Possible euphemism for that is a serious crime

parts.note: SC is scilicet, Latin for namely or that is
rape is a grave criminal offence

explanation.surface: Someone soft-pedals a grave offence with a gentle word.
explanation.walkthrough: SC is the scholarly abbreviation of scilicet, 'namely'. A 'scrape' with the law is a mild way of describing trouble.
explanation.definitionFit: Getting into a scrape is a mild idiom for trouble, which might understate an offence.

clue.text: Plant gives point to endless show of contempt

parts.note: S, south, is a compass point

indicators.note: the synonym has its final letter cut off

parts.note: an affront is an open insult

explanation.surface: A plant hints at endless scorn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' cuts the T from AFFRONT to leave AFFRON.
explanation.definitionFit: Saffron is a crocus whose stigmas give the costly yellow spice.

clue.text: Abandon in capital

definitions.meaning: to leave someone stuck and helpless
a famous street in London, the capital

explanation.walkthrough: The Strand is a major street in central London.
explanation.definitionFit: To strand is to leave stranded; the Strand is a well-known London thoroughfare.

clue.text: St Paul's intended receiver, according to Spooner

indicators.note: the swap of opening sounds named after the Reverend Spooner

parts.note: meant means intended
a taker is someone who receives

explanation.surface: The person St Paul meant to receive his letter.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of MEANT TAKER gives the sound of TENT MAKER. The Book of Acts says Paul made tents for a living.
explanation.definitionFit: Paul's trade, according to Acts 18, was making tents.

clue.text: Chop up a number among 6 victims

indicators.note: among puts the letter in the middle of the other word

parts.note: the victims of a 6-down, a mousetrap, are mice
N is a symbol for an unspecified number

explanation.surface: Some of a trap's victims get chopped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'among' puts N inside MICE; '6' points back to 6-down.
explanation.definitionFit: To mince is to cut food into very small pieces.

clue.text: Sort of case made of fibre

indicators.note: made of says the answer is built from these letters in another order

explanation.surface: A kind of bag woven from fibre.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made of' rearranges FIBRE.
explanation.definitionFit: A briefcase is a type of case, so brief names that sort.

clue.text: The question of having children?

definitions.meaning: the matter under debate, the point at stake
offspring, as in dying without heirs

explanation.definitionFit: Issue is both a point in dispute and a legal word for a person's offspring.

clue.text: Race of Mary and Joseph?

indicators.note: the answer is made of a run of letters inside these names

explanation.surface: Asking the ethnic origin of the Holy Family.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'Mary and'. The question mark nods to the irony, since Mary and Joseph were Jewish.
explanation.definitionFit: The term once named the Indo-European peoples, later twisted by Nazi racial theory.

clue.text: Work on paper or for slave-driver

indicators.note: on here means placed next to, so the work comes directly before the paper

parts.note: OP, opus, is a musical work
the press is the newspapers

explanation.surface: Working on a newspaper for a tyrannical boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces run OP, PRESS, OR.
explanation.definitionFit: An oppressor is a cruel taskmaster, one who holds others down.

clue.text: Resentment put on over 5 losing head

indicators.note: the word for put on is placed around the shortened name, covering it

parts.note: to don clothes is to put them on

indicators.note: the Dickens name drops its first letter

parts.note: the answer to 5-down, the Dickens character

explanation.surface: Bitterness is assumed about a decapitated figure.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' points to the Dickens answer at 5-down; 'losing head' drops its first letter and 'over' wraps the clothing verb around what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Dudgeon means indignation, as in going off in high dudgeon.

clue.text: Send to gulag reportedly one by one

indicators.note: reportedly says the word is heard rather than written

parts.note: in turn means one after another

explanation.surface: Prisoners sent to the camps one at a time.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TURN, said out loud, gives the answer's sound.
explanation.definitionFit: To intern is to imprison or confine, as in a Soviet gulag camp.
